A second case shows the planted `gov` answers the store of the folder it runs in, so the first case cannot pass for the wrong reason. Driver cases check the children's `--repo` and `--store` on both paths, and that the fresh path still starts its launch steps.
  - **F-B:** a commit lands during the planted scan and the remote keeps the scanned commit; the next cycle pushes the late commit after its own scan; a missing branch and a branch made during the scan push nothing.
  - **R1:** four ACT cases, with `shutil.which` stood in.
  - The planted `gov`'s `store_from_cwd` mode answers the fingerprints head of `<--root or cwd>/.gov-runtime/store.db`.
- **discoveries:**
  - (1) On the fresh path, the `pool` child still gets the repository as `--repo`, so its retrieval-only re-measure searches the repository's own store. The brief named three children, so I left it.
  - (2) No W2-172 case pinned the repository as the children's root; all green.
  - (3) An untracked, empty `pytest-of-usain/` folder (one `.lock-held`, 12K) appeared in the worktree root at 20:31:12, while `tests/unit/memaudit` and `tests/acceptance/W2-187` were both running. It is not committed and not deleted (I may only `rm` inside my TMPDIR). I could not tell which run made it.
- **risks:**
  - The link is used as given (a symlink). If a rebuild flips it to the other half in the middle of a run, later searches answer the new commit and the run faults (`STOPPED fault`). It fails closed.
  - The children now run `git` (ls-tree, diff, grep) in the link. That works because the integration halves are worktrees of the same repository and share its objects.
- **lessons:** A stand-in that answers a fixed store commit cannot show which store was reached. A planted `gov` that answers from its cwd's store closes that gap.
- **proposed_decisions:** Whether the fresh path's `pool` child should also work in the link, so the pool figures come from the declared store too. My recommendation is yes, as a follow-up; confidence medium.
